1.pericope_label: Then I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a flying roll. And he said unto me, What seest thou? And I answered, I see a flying roll; the length thereof is twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof ten cubits. Then said he unto me, This is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth: for every one that stealeth shall be cut off as on this side according to it; and every one that sweareth shall be cut off as on that side according to it. I will bring it forth, saith the Lord of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.

schools.summary: Take the two figures as one vision, restrict the curse to the land of Israel, and find in the roll's dimensions the measure of the sanctuary applied to sin.
Identify the curse with the written law and charge previous interpreters with missing the design of the Spirit altogether.
Divide the chapter into two visions, refer the crimes to the Chaldeans, and leave the extent of the curse open between Judea and the world.
Notes that the prophet needed no waking this time, and reads the written curse as answering to the written command of the law.

debates.question: Whose crimes are recorded on the roll?

positions.position: The Chaldeans': the house the curse enters is Babylon, city of a public plunderer and glaring idolater.
Israel's: the phrase means the whole land, not the whole earth.
Left open between the land of Judea and all the world, wherever these sins are found.
Whatever evils the Jews suffered proceeded from the righteous judgment of God.

debates.question: Does the chapter contain one vision or two?

positions.position: Two: the flying roll with its explanation, and then the ephah with the woman.
One: the figures are too closely connected to divide, and the pause between the views is no sufficient reason for assuming otherwise.

outliers.claim: Observes that the roll's dimensions are those of the holy place and of the temple porch, so that the measure of the sanctuary is the measure of sin, and the sinner must not plead that he is no worse than his neighbour.

Charges that interpreters have touched neither heaven nor earth in explaining this prophecy because they have not regarded the design of the Holy Spirit, rejecting in particular the view that the volume means corrupt glosses on doctrine.

themes: Then I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a flying roll.

5.pericope_label: Then the angel that talked with me went forth, and said unto me, Lift up now thine eyes, and see what is this that goeth forth. And I said, What is it? And he said, This is an ephah that goeth forth. He said moreover, This is their resemblance through all the earth. And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and this is a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah. And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof. Then lifted I up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven. Then said I to the angel that talked with me, Whither do these bear the ephah? And he said unto me, To build it an house in the land of Shinar: and it shall be established, and set there upon her own base.

schools.summary: Reads the angel's going forth as emergence from the invisible, declines to press the details of the winged women, and takes the ephah for the gathering of individual sinners.
Supplies the weights of the talent exactly and applies the woman to the Roman antichrist rather than to the Jewish nation.
Make the woman the wickedness of the Jews and read Shinar as Rome, the captivity continuing to the present day.
Explains the vision's obscurity as deliberate, lest a plain denunciation of the second overthrow discourage the present restoration.

debates.question: What does the woman in the ephah represent?

positions.position: The impiety of the Jewish nation, the mass of its iniquity, with the lead as the wrath of God bending it down.
A symbol of the sinners named in the previous vision, gathered as separate grains are gathered in a measure.
The Roman antichrist, whose title is his Holiness but whose proper name is wickedness.

debates.question: Where is the ephah carried, and what does it mean?

positions.position: To Babylon, the carrying denoting the cause of the captivity, the measure of sins filled up.
Shinar means Babylon and Babylon means Rome, so the house signifies a long captivity under the Romans which remains to this day.
Babylon, whither many fled and others were driven by the Romans, to be confined without hope of release upon the lees of their own unbelief.

outliers.claim: Explains the deliberate obscurity of the vision, citing an earlier expositor by name, as intended to keep a plain denunciation of the second overthrow of temple and state from discouraging the present restoration of both.

Declines to press the minute details of the winged women, holding that they are probably introduced merely to give the picture distinctness, and suggests the prophet borrowed the imagery from grotesque figures seen in Babylon.
